generation.raw_text: {"status":"answered","answer":"In a food chain, the amount of energy transferred from one step to the next decreases significantly. This is because only a small proportion of the energy consumed by organisms is converted into new tissue, which forms the food for the next trophic level. Most of the energy is used for staying alive, such as in respiration, or is lost as waste. Typically, only about 10% of the energy is transferred to the next level, making energy transfer in food chains relatively inefficient.","selected_evidence_ids":["E1"],"citations":[{"evidence_id":"E1","pdf_page":220,"textbook_page":211}],"missing_information":[]}
